articles.title: Thousands without shelter face lethal conditions in storm-hit Gaza as they wait for 150,000 tents
articles.summary:
Charities warn of lack of protection amid health fears for more than 940,000 displaced people living in flood-prone areas

Tens of thousands of Palestinians have been left in waterlogged and…

blocks.text: Tens of thousands of Palestinians have been left in waterlogged and damaged tents after deadly storms at the weekend, while 150,000 new shelters are held outside Gaza awaiting Israeli approval to enter, aid agencies have said.

At least four Palestinian children and woman were killed as heavy rains and wind battered fragile, leaky tents. Thousands have been left without shelter and sanitation infrastructure has been destroyed, with sewage spewing into people’s tents.
“All our clothes were soaked. My kids are all sick and I can’t afford to buy them more clothes,” said Raed Jamal, a displaced Palestinian. “Watching them suffering in the cold is heartbreaking.”

blocks.caption: Storm winds rattles tents for displaced Palestinians on Gaza’s coast

blocks.text: “These conditions are so difficult, the whole night I had to use pots to collect rainwater because it was falling on us.”
He shared videos with the Guardian of his tent shaking in the wind as rain poured through holes in its roof.
Aid workers warn disease will spread rapidly unless families are quickly supplied with new shelters and ways to keep warm.

blocks.caption: Displaced Palestinians repair storm-damaged tents in western Gaza City last week. Photograph: Mohammed Salha/APAImages/Shutterstock

blocks.text: The UK-based charity Medical Aid for Palestinians said it was concerned about a rise in health problems because families were living in flooded tents with nowhere else to go.

“Our medical teams expect to see more respiratory illnesses and other health complications linked to cold, damp and overcrowded conditions, and we fear more children could die from hypothermia, as happened last winter,” said Mai Elawawda, MAP’s communications officer in Gaza.

According to the UN, 940,000 people in Gaza are in areas at risk of flooding in makeshift tents without protection from heavy rainfall. The flooding threat has been heightened as facilities for pumping out storm water are not operating due to a lack of power.

Shelterbox, a charity working in humanitarian crisis zones, said the tents it usually supplies during emergencies have been waiting outside Gaza for almost two years and it has instead been forced to improvise shelters built from tarpaulins and wooden pallets. But even these materials, it says, are being restricted.
“The latest devastating floods impacting displaced people in Gaza demonstrate exactly why more durable improvements to shelter are desperately needed ahead of winter,” said a Shelterbox spokesperson.

“The over-reliance on emergency solutions, rather than building shelters from more robust materials, means that many people are living in shelters that are simply not suitable to withstand the weather conditions that the region experiences and will quickly deteriorate.”

blocks.caption: Palestinians inspect tents buried under rocks and earth a day after a large sandstone slab collapsed at a displacement camp, killing at least five people in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza Strip. Photograph: Abdel Kareem Hana/AP

blocks.text: A child drowned in flood waters and at least three children and their mother died when a sand dune fell on their tent at the weekend, according to the Palestinian health ministry.
The UN said 26,000 households had sought its help after the rains and at least 3,900 households were now without shelter at all.

Palestinians in Gaza are facing their second winter since a ceasefire was agreed more than a year ago, but aid workers said conditions were no better than last year because of Israeli restrictions on “dual-use items” and backlogs at crossings were limiting critical supplies to build shelters.

“It’s very difficult to deal with it because there’s also there’s no clear process for things. There’s a level of capriciousness that one day toolkits will be allowed in, another day toolkits will not and they don’t say why,” said Sheltherbox the spokesperson.

The Council for Arab-British Understanding (Caabu) has called on the British government to pressure Israel to allow supplies into Gaza and reverse restrictions on humanitarian workers, including restoring the licences of dozens of organisations, such as Médecins Sans Frontières, Oxfam and the Norwegian Refugee Council.

blocks.caption: Employees and workers of the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees (UNRWA) hold placards during a protest in Khan Younis, southern Gaza Strip, 9 November. Photograph: Tariq Mohammad/APAImages/Shutterstock

blocks.text: “The predictable winter rains and floods have, as warned about, battered already devastated Palestinians, where disease and malnutrition is rife, and a basic tent blocked by Israel is a manmade and political scarcity,” said Caabu’s head of parliamentary affairs, Joseph Willits. “A lack of political action isn’t something a Palestinian family trying to shelter from Gaza’s floods can afford.”

Israel claimed last week to have allowed 10,000 tents into Gaza, but that falls far short of the number needed – the UN said 150,000 were waiting outside Gaza for entry for the estimated 94% of Palestinians in Gaza who need help finding shelter.

The Israeli NGO Gisha, which lobbies for goods and people to be able to enter and exit Gaza more freely, said the Israeli authorities had enforced stricter limits on goods entering Gaza than in previous ceasefires.

blocks.caption: A Palestinian child shows the inside of his family’s tent during a storm in Gaza

blocks.text: While the Israeli authorities claim to be allowing an average of 600 trucks into Gaza each day, they count 12 pallets of goods as a single truck, even though a truck usually carries about 20 pallets – which could amount to about a 40% reduction on what could be carried into Gaza. Gisha has also accused Israeli authorities of a lack of transparency on what is being allowed to enter Gaza.

Nour al-Batsh, the mother of a seven-month-old child, said she was forced to rent a partially destroyed apartment she shares with others for $500 a month, relying on donations from abroad, after her tent collapsed.

“The cold is lethal. Living in a tent by the sea means facing the constant threat of death from the freezing temperatures,” said Batsh, who can see her old tent from her current shelter. “We are still in autumn, and winter has not even properly begun. I look at my fragile tent and I beg God that I will not have to go back to it. Because death inside that tent is certain.”

articles.title: Thousands of rare wildflowers rescued from eroding Scottish coast
articles.summary:
Conservationists relocate 3,400 one-flowered wintergreens, a species estimated to have lost more than half its UK population in the past 50 years

Thousands of one of Britain’s rarest…

blocks.text: Thousands of one of Britain’s rarest wildflowers have been moved to safety from an eroding Scottish shoreline where they were at risk of falling into the sea.

Conservationists rescued 3,400 one-flowered wintergreen plants at Culbin Forest in Moray, in an effort to protect a species estimated to have lost more than half its UK population in the past 50 years.

“We don’t yet know how many plants will survive at their new home in Culbin Forest, but we do know that it was only a matter of time before they would have all been lost to the sea if we’d left them where they were,” said Iain Macdonald, a biodiversity adviser at NatureScot.

In the UK, the tiny, star-shaped wildflower is found only in pine woods in north-east Scotland. It survives at just seven sites, only three of which support healthy populations, according to Plantlife Scotland.

blocks.caption: The one-flowered wintergreen plant has lost more than half its UK population in the past 50 years. Photograph: NatureScot/Richard Spowart

blocks.text: The charity worked with Forestry and Land Scotland, NatureScot and volunteers to relocate the plants after 2-3 metres of land collapsed into the sea over recent years.
Sam Jones, senior ecological adviser at Plantlife Scotland, said: “This type of groundbreaking conservation work will help ensure endangered species like the one-flowered wintergreen are not lost.”

Translocating the flowers meant uprooting their underground support systems. Volunteers cut out sections of soil around the plants to preserve the networks of fungi on which they depend for germination and survival.

blocks.caption: The translocation of a one-flowered wintergreen. Photograph: NatureScot/Richard Spowart

blocks.text: Alongside obtaining energy through photosynthesis, one-flowered wintergreen can draw energy from fungi in woodland soils, a relationship that has complicated efforts to understand and reverse its decline.

Changes in forest management have affected the conditions those fungi need, while hotter, drier conditions caused by the climate crisis have reduced the soil moisture on which the plant relies, Plantlife said.

Although an estimated 50,000 plants remain in Scotland, they spread by producing genetically identical growth through their roots. The number of genetically distinct individuals could be fewer than 500. At one site, about 100 plants represented just two distinct individuals.

blocks.caption: Translocation of a one-flowered wintergreen. Photograph: NatureScot/Richard Spowart

blocks.text: Eighteen volunteers conducted the rescue, which followed a smaller trial. The project received support from the Scottish government’s nature restoration fund.
Conservationists have also moved a small number of plants and seeds to another wood, where the species has not previously been recorded, hoping to establish a new population.

Macdonald said: “Any survival will be a success, and if we can continue to introduce more plants to some of the small, existing populations then we’ll strengthen their ability to cope with our changing environment.”

articles.title: Fresh concerns raised over Gaza doctor held by Israel for 23 months without charge
articles.summary:
Independent Israeli professor says Hussam Abu Safiya’s life will be at risk until he receives proper medical treatment

An independent professor who reviewed the medical records of a…

blocks.text: An independent professor who reviewed the medical records of a prominent Gaza doctor held in an Israeli prison without charge for nearly 23 months has raised serious concerns about his health.
Hussam Abu Safiya was detained at work on 27 December 2024 and later held in solitary confinement at Rakefet, a notorious underground prison.

During a visit by a lawyer from Physicians for Human Rights Israel (PHRI) in the summer, the doctor told of harsh conditions, untreated medical problems and severe food shortages. Witnesses said he had become almost unrecognisable.
Nearly 700 days after his arrest, Israeli authorities have yet to bring any formal charges against Abu Safiya, who is the director of Kamal Adwan hospital in northern Gaza.
He was classified as an “unlawful combatant” along with more than 375 medical workers – a designation Israel has used to justify prolonged detention without trial.

Last month, Israel’s supreme court rejected a petition to release the doctor. Over the weekend, a district court rejected a separate petition to allow Abu Safiya an independent medical examination, despite troubling findings in his medical records that were not adequately investigated, according to Prof Amit Tirosh, an independent Israeli specialist who reviewed a file obtained by PHRI.

blocks.caption: Hussam Abu Safiya, right, shows a UN delegation around the Kamal Adwan hospital in northern Gaza in September 2024. His family have not been able to communicate with him directly in detention. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

blocks.text: In an interview with the Guardian, Tirosh said Abu Safiya’s weight had fallen from 90kg (14st 2lb) in January 2025 to 76kg this May.
“Continuous food deprivation and weight loss, repeated beatings and injuries, with inadequate medical care, can definitely cost Dr Abu Safiya his life,” Tirosh said.
“According to PHRI records, more than 100 prisoners died in Israeli facilities between 2023 and 2025 … a threat to his life unfortunately cannot be ruled out.”
Tirosh identified insufficient investigation of chest pain, delays in treating scabies and a drop in haemoglobin levels that warranted further examination.

“A 14kg weight loss is very alarming, even more so if the cause is unknown,” he added. “More troubling, the medical team was neither surprised nor concerned: one prison physician wrote that his weight loss over a year is ‘a common trend among security prisoners associated to their diet’.
“Haemoglobin dropped between February and July 2026, long after the weight loss, so detention or starvation alone cannot explain it; it coincided with the reported beatings in Rakefet.
“Such blood loss can be life-threatening and requires urgent ER evaluation. Per the records, these urgent problems were not addressed and could endanger his life.”

Medical records documented bruising around one of Abu Safiya’s eyes, dizziness and rib pain in July. He told his lawyers he had been beaten by prison guards but Tirosh said the records did not explain his injuries.

The district court ruling also revealed allegations made by Israeli authorities that Abu Safiya had exaggerated his medical problems, set up organisations from prison, influenced other prisoners and maintained international contacts.
PHRI said the Israeli allegations did not justify denying him an independent medical examination, a right protected by law.
“The bottom line is that a third party should see him and the full medical records,” said Tirosh. ‘‘Refusing an independent examination is never justified.

“To the Israeli prison system authorities I would say that I feel deep shame to be counted with them as a doctor or health provider in Israel. As a system, they betray every medical and ethical principle I stand for.”
The Israeli prison service did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Abu Safiya had become the face of health workers struggling to treat patients throughout the war in Gaza before his detention. He is being held indefinitely, along with thousands of other Palestinian civilians, in prisons that Israeli rights groups say have become torture camps.
At the time of his arrest at work, Abu Safiya was wearing a white medical coat that he had refused to wash since his son, Ibrahim, was killed by a drone strike at the hospital entrance that October.
Abu Safiya had helped keep the hospital running through more than 80 days of siege and attacks by Israeli forces amid an intensive military operation in the surrounding refugee camp.

“Fourteen Palestinian doctors, including hospital directors and specialists in essential medical fields, remain imprisoned without charge or trial at a time when Gaza’s healthcare system desperately needs them,” said Naji Abbas of PHRI.

A spokesperson for the Israeli prison service (IPS) told the Guardian the allegations are “part of a broader campaign aimed at discrediting the state of Israel” and that the IPS “operates in accordance with the law and under constant judicial oversight”.
Abu Safiya’s family have not been able to communicate with him directly in detention.

articles.title: Youpla directors disqualified over collapsed funeral fund that targeted Aboriginal families
articles.summary:
Three directors were fined a combined $90,000 in federal court judgment and disqualified from managing a corporation for between five and 10 years

  • Get our

blocks.text: Three directors of a collapsed funeral fund that marketed insurance to Aboriginal families have been banned from managing corporations for at least five years and ordered to pay a combined $90,000 after being found to have breached their duties to clients.

On Wednesday, federal court justice Geoffrey Kennett ordered the former director of the insurance company Youpla Group, previously the Aboriginal Community Benefit Fund (ACBF), Jonathan Law, to pay the commonwealth $50,000 and disqualified him from managing corporations for six years.

Michael Wilson, also a director, was ordered to pay $20,000 and disqualified from managing corporations for 10 years, while director Geoffrey Clayton was ordered to pay $20,000 and disqualified from managing corporations for five years.

The trio were also ordered to pay a combined $17,000 towards plaintiff’s costs. Kennett found they had failed to perform their duties with the degree of “care and diligence” expected, failed to manage conflicts of interest, and caused a detriment to the ACBF members.

It followed a judgment late last month where the founder of the company, Ron Pattenden, was ordered to pay a quarter of a million dollars and barred from managing corporations for 15 years. Pattenden acknowledged he had breached directors’ duties in a claim settlement with financial watchdog, the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC).

During the same judgment, the former Youpla Group chief Bryn Jones was found by Kennett to have breached his directorial duties after a contested liability hearing in February. He denied having knowledge of the fund’s insurance premium increases. Jones’s penalty will be determined at a hearing at a later date.
Youpla sold junk funeral policies to Indigenous people across Australia for decades, including targeting communities where English was not the first language and communities with low literacy levels.

It collapsed in March 2022, leaving more than 13,000 Aboriginal people, some elderly and in palliative care, without the means to pay for funerals. Families had to resort to crowdfunding and some were forced to leave their loved ones’ bodies in the morgue while they raised the funds.

In August 2023, Asic commenced proceedings in federal court against the five former directors and officers for breaches of their duties, alleging governance failures and director misconduct that affected the First Nations people who were members of the funds.

It alleged the directors and officers maintained insurance arrangements with Crown Insurance, a Vanuatu-based company owned and controlled by Pattenden and another director, Law, and did not act in the best interest of the ACBF entities and members.
Breaches of directors’ duties can attract a maximum penalty of $200,000 for each breach that occurred between 2017 and March 2019.

Youpla targeted Indigenous people using marketing materials in the distinctive red, black and yellow colours of the Aboriginal flag, including stuffed toys and colouring books for children, turning up to community events and by conducting door-to-door sales.
after newsletter promotion
It was investigated by various regulators over the years but it was not until 2018, when its conduct was exposed in the banking royal commission, that its licence to sell new products was withdrawn.
In 2021 Asic questioned its solvency, and the company’s directors finally pulled the plug.

The federal court handed Youpla a $1.2m fine in September 2023 for misrepresenting junk funeral policies, finding it had told plan holders they would receive a lump sum payment when in fact they would only be reimbursed for expenses they could prove had been incurred.
Youpla avoided paying millions more in fines handed down by the federal court in July 2025 because it was in liquidation.
A $97m federal government support package was announced in February 2024 to help thousands of mostly low-income Aboriginal families recover from financial loss.

The government’s payments to remaining victims will continue to be processed until 1 December this year. Eligible recipients have the choice of a funeral bond or a cash payment worth 60% of the value of their policy.
– with Australian Associated Press.

articles.title: Spain demands that TikTok suspend operations until child sexual abuse material gone
articles.summary: Spain's Youth Minister Sira Rego appeals to prosecutors and the Data Protection Agency to take action against the social media company

blocks.text: TIKTOK. Teenagers pose for a photo while holding smartphones in front of a TikTok logo in this illustration taken September 11, 2025
Dado Ruvic/Reuters
Spain's Youth Minister Sira Rego appeals to prosecutors and the Data Protection Agency to take action against the social media company

MADRID, Spain – Spain’s government has demanded that TikTok suspend its operations in Spain until it eliminates child sexual abuse material, it said on Tuesday, November 10, after a media report documented 1,183 explicit posts on the platform with millions of views.

Youth Minister Sira Rego, whose ministry cannot singlehandedly ban the platform in Spain, has appealed to prosecutors and the Data Protection Agency to take action against the social media company, according to a statement by the ministry.
“Social media cannot be lawless territory,” Rego said.

The request comes months after Sanchez’s government requested a probe into X, Meta, and TikTok for allegedly spreading AI-generated child sexual abuse material, as European regulators intensify scrutiny of big tech over harmful and illegal content.
TikTok did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

Spanish fact-checking nonprofit Maldita.es on Monday published an investigation revealing that videos of explicit child sexual abuse had been viewed on the platform at least 48 million times, with over 26,000 profiles commenting on and sharing the material.

The organization published a follow-up story on Tuesday evening stating that TikTok had restricted two of the search terms that Maldita.es’s investigation identified as pathways to child sexual abuse content for users in Spain, but that searches from other European countries still led to the same content. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Who is Tristan Domingo, the Davao official behind contracts awarded to Duterte’s company?
articles.summary: Domingo has long been serving Davao City in various capacities under the Duterte political dynasty

blocks.text: DAVAO AIDE. Davao City Assistant Administrator Tristan Dwight Domingo delivers a speech during the demonstration of the eDriver operating system at the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board headquarters in Bago Gallera on January 31, 2023.
Davao City Hall
Domingo has long been serving Davao City in various capacities under the Duterte political dynasty

items: Davao City Hall awarded food contracts worth millions of pesos to Gencorp Industries Inc., linked to Vice President Sara Duterte, signed by assistant city administrator Tristan Dwight P. Domingo instead of Mayor Baste Duterte.

The procurement process raises concerns about potential conflicts of interest, as Domingo was appointed by Sara Duterte when she was mayor, and he has significant authority in the city's procurement regulations.
Mayor Baste Duterte stated that he was unaware of any interest Sara Duterte had in Gencorp and insisted that all transactions followed government procurement laws.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Millions of pesos worth of food contracts awarded by Davao City Hall to a company linked to Vice President Sara Duterte were signed not by Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte, but by an assistant city administrator entrusted with exercising the mayor’s authority.

Tristan Dwight P. Domingo, Davao City’s assistant city administrator for administration, signed contracts awarded to Gencorp Industries Inc., a company declared in the Vice President’s Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN).

The transactions raise questions about the city’s procurement process and potential conflicts of interest, particularly because the contracts were awarded under the administration of Baste Duterte, Sara’s brother.
Last September, Rappler’s investigative report found that Gencorp secured millions of pesos worth of food supply contracts from Davao City Hall.
One of the contracts obtained by Rappler cited Executive Order No. 28, dated July 1, 2022, as the basis for Domingo’s authority to sign on behalf of the mayor.
Domingo’s LinkedIn profile identifies him as the duly authorized representative of the city mayor and the head of the procuring entity (HOPE).
“As the HOPE, he is responsible for approving or disapproving BAC (Bidding and Awards Committee) recommendations and ensuring adherence to procurement regulations,” his profile reads.

During the impeachment trial of the Vice President, Mayor Baste Duterte, standing as a witness, said he delegated the authority to sign contracts to Domingo so he could attend to other responsibilities as mayor.

In a statement released in September following Rappler’s investigation, Mayor Duterte said he and all other officials and employees of the Davao City Hall “never had any knowledge of Vice President Sara Z. Duterte holding an interest in Gencorp.” Baste maintained that all of the transactions of the city government with Gencorp follow government procurement laws.
Domingo’s position in Davao City’s bureaucracy predates Baste Duterte’s current mayoral post.
In 2013, when Sara Duterte was still mayor, she appointed Domingo as assistant city administrator, according to a SunStar report. His appointment came a day before Duterte went on maternity leave.
Before his appointment, Domingo served as acting chief of the Davao City Business Bureau.

In 2016, Duterte even gave Domingo power to file charges “against any official or employee of the city who may have committed an offense in the performance of his officials duties, and functions,” according to a Philstar report.

The Duterte family has been running Davao City Hall for nearly four decades. Rodrigo Duterte served as mayor for several terms starting in 1988 before Sara Duterte succeeded him. Sara served as vice mayor from 2007 to 2010, mayor from 2010 to 2013, and from 2016 to 2022. In 2022, she was elected as the country’s vice president.
Beyond his position as assistant city administrator, Domingo also serves as the Davao City government’s data protection officer, according to his LinkedIn profile.

He is also listed as project manager for two of the city’s flagship initiatives: the Davao Public Transport Modernization Project, also known as the Davao Bus Project or High Priority Bus System, and construction of waste-to-energy facilities.
Domingo is a lawyer who earned his law degree from Ateneo de Davao University. He studied political science and sociology at the University of the Philippines Baguio.– Rappler.com

articles.title: Ex-OFW turns Laguna footwear into thriving community business
articles.summary: Elizabeth Francisco Consebido's enterprise in Liliw, Laguna, supports local artisans and preserves the town's rich slipper-making tradition

blocks.text: ENTERPRISE. Elizabeth Fashion Footwear's store in Liliw, Laguna, helps keep the hometown industry alive.
Department of Trade and Industry
Elizabeth Francisco Consebido's enterprise in Liliw, Laguna, supports local artisans and preserves the town's rich slipper-making tradition
This is a feature release from the Department of Trade and Industry’s Office of the Undersecretary for Regional Operations Group.

Known for skilled craftsmanship and vibrant slipper-making heritage, Liliw, Laguna, has long been home to dedicated footwear artisans. Among those who saw a vital opportunity to support this local tradition is Elizabeth Francisco Consebido, a former accountant who worked in Saudi Arabia.

When the pandemic hit, Elizabeth witnessed the heavy toll it took on local businesses and workers in her community. Motivated by a desire to help artisans sustain their livelihoods beyond just generating personal income, she established Elizabeth Fashion Footwear (EFF Footwear Store) on October 15, 2021.

blocks.caption: RECOGNITION. Former OFW-turned-entrepreneur Elizabeth Consebido is recognized by the DTI at the MSME Summit. Department of Trade and Industry photo

blocks.text: Driven by a purpose, she launched the business with an initial capital of P70,000. She allocated P50,000 toward raw materials — such as fabric, rubber, foam and adhesive — along with labor costs, and invested P20,000 in essential equipment, including a second-hand sewing machine and a sole-finishing machine. She then rented a storefront along Gat Tayaw Street in Barangay Pag-Asa in Liliw, selling locally crafted slippers known as “lightweight.”

During its early operations, EFF produced over 500 pairs of slippers weekly. Elizabeth sold them at the store P80 per pair while supplying nearby retailers at a wholesale price of P65 to broaden her reach and build a strong retail network.

Building the enterprise, however, came with challenges. Low initial sales, mounting operating expenses, and stiff competition from cheap imported footwear placed immense pressure on the business. There were moments when Elizabeth considered giving up, but knowing her workers and their families on EFF gave her the strength to persevere. Keeping the business afloat was about protecting both her vision and the livelihoods of her team.

Determined to adapt, she expanded her reach through online selling on Shopee, Lazada and TikTok. She also actively participated in small-business initiatives led by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), including the Kapatid Mentor ME (KMME) Program; One Town, One Product (OTOP) Program and various business development seminars. Through KMME, she gained practical skills in financial management, product costing, branding and strategic planning.

blocks.caption: MARKETING. Elizabeth Fashion Footwear joins the Kadiwa ng Pangulo initiative. Department of Trade and Industry photo

blocks.text: DTI further opened commercial doors for EFF Footwear Store by featuring its products in trade fairs, bazaars and the Kadiwa ng Pangulo initiative, allowing Elizabeth to showcase local footwear craftsmanship to broader markets.

To meet rising demand, the enterprise acquired a hydraulic pressing machine to streamline the cutting of rubber soles. This single upgrade tripled weekly production from 500 to 1,500 pairs, giving Elizabeth the confidence to accept bulk orders with tight deadlines and expand her product line to include doll shoes, sandals and fresh slipper designs.

EFF Footwear Store’s steady growth has drawn widespread recognition. The business earned a Silver Award under the Likhang Laguna Quality Standards, was featured on DZME Radio’s “Pro Pinoy” program with Melanie Sembrano, and received support through the BPI Foundation’s Sinag Beyond Program.
In December 2025, EFF showcased its signature abaca-adorned espadrilles and floral canvas half-shoes with wooden heels at the DTI National Trade Fair held at SM Megamall.

From a team of just four employees at its start, EFF Footwear Store now provides steady employment for eight local artisans. For Elizabeth, the people behind the products remain the heart of her journey.

Today, EFF Footwear Store stands as a clear example of how perseverance, strategic growth, and a commitment to community can turn a modest investment into a thriving, purpose-driven enterprise. – Rappler.com

MANILA, Philippines — The Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) has opened applications for the Supreme Court associate justice seat vacated by Rodil Zalameda following his appointment as chief justice on November 5.
Applicants have until December 28 at 4:30 p.m. to submit their applications.

articles.title: Slovak top envoy Juraj Blanar to visit PH on Nov. 12-15, 2026
articles.summary: Slovak Minister of Foreign and European Affairs Juraj Blanar will be in the Philippines from November 12 to 15 for an official visit.

blocks.text: Published November 11, 2026 12:07pm
Slovak Minister of Foreign and European Affairs Juraj Blanar will be in the Philippines from November 12 to 15 for an official visit.
In a statement on Tuesday, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) said this marks the first official visit by a Slovak foreign minister to the Philippines since 2015.
Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro will hold a bilateral meeting and luncheon with Blanar on Thursday, November 12.
Blanar and Lazaro are expected to discuss bilateral cooperation in political and economic relations as well as people-to-people ties.
The two officials will also exchange views on regional and international issues.
DFA said this marks the third meeting between Lazaro and Blanar, who also met at the 4th European Union Indo-Pacific Ministerial Forum in Brussels last November 2025.
They also met during the 25th Association of Southeast Asian Nations — European Union (ASEAN-EU) Ministerial Meeting in April 2026 in Brunei.
Blanar will keynote the Philippine-Slovak Business Forum on Friday, November 13.

Traveling with a business delegation, the Slovak official will also meet with Trade and Industry Secretary Cristina Roque to discuss joint efforts to enhancd trade and investment between the countries.

Blanar will officially open the Slovak Embassy in Manila and sign the Declaration of the Deposit of the Slovak Republic's Instrument of Accession to the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia.
The DFA said the accession provides a framework for stronger Slovak engagement with ASEAN in line with the country's Strategic Concept on the Indo-Pacific, which was launched in 2025.
There are around 3,600 Filipinos in Slovakia. In 2025, bilatetal trade between the two nations amounted to $29.74 million. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: David Jones to close half its stores triggering mass job losses under ‘urgent restructure’
articles.summary:
Australia’s oldest department store collapsed into voluntary administration last week after years of steep losses

David Jones is set to shutter half its department store network, triggering…

blocks.text: David Jones is set to shutter half its department store network, triggering mass job losses under a sweeping restructure, receivers FTI Consulting said on Wednesday.
David Jones employs more than 6,000 staff across 38 stores.
FTI said in a statement that it would proceed with an “urgent restructure of the business”.
“As part of this restructure, the receivers have commenced an immediate consultation process for all staff associated with 19 stores that have been identified for closure,” FTI said.
“For the immediate term these stores will continue trading and while there is no final date for the closures, we anticipate they will cease trading by the end of the year.”
Under a dual appointment, receivers FTI has day-to-day control of operations, while administrators McGrathNicol seek a buyer or fresh injection of capital.
The upheaval follows years of steep losses after the retailer failed to carve out a profitable niche in a sector disrupted by online competitors and stand-alone upmarket stores.
The department store collapsed into voluntary administration last week.
In documents released late on Tuesday, David Jones’s administrators revealed they reviewed the private equity-owned department chain’s finances months before it fell into administration.
Some small suppliers are owed money dating back to stock sent in April, well before David Jones missed rent payments and fell into administration.
after newsletter promotion

Its private equity owner, Anchorage Capital, has long sought a slimmed down version of David Jones, free from long-term leases on underperforming sites. It is expected to make a proposal to administrators to re-purchase the 188-year-old chain.

The following stores will be closed: Carousel, WA, Garden City, WA, Glen Waverley, VIC, Green Hills, NSW, Hay Street Mall, WA, Highpoint, VIC, Hornsby, NSW, Macarthur Square, NSW, Macquarie Centre, NSW, Malvern Central, VIC, Marion, SA, Newmarket, NZ, Parramatta, NSW, Robina Town Centre, QLD, Sunshine Plaza, QLD, Warringah Mall, NSW, West Lakes, SA, Woden, ACT, Wollongong Central, NSW.

blocks.text: Published November 11, 2026 11:52am
Vice President Sara Duterte is not a stock holder of Gencorp Industries, Inc., one of the Vice President’s declared business interests, a defense witness said Wednesday.

Atty. Suzette Balucanag-Punay, the in-house counsel of Gencorp Industries, Inc. and Metro City Chow Foods Corporation, made the testimony during Day 42 of the impeachment of Vice President Duterte based on the corporate records of Gencorp Industries, Inc.

During the direct examination of defense counsel Justin Gular, Punay said the Vice President’s name did not appear on the General Information Sheets (GIS) Gencorp Industries, Inc. from 2022 to 2025 or the years when she was already the Vice President.
“She has no stockholdings with GenCorp.,” Punay said.
Punay also said that the Vice President also did not have shareholdings or positions held in Gencorp Industries, Inc. from 2022 to 2025.
Likewise, Punay said the Vice President did not receive dividends in those years since there were no dividends declared by Gencorp Industries, Inc.

The Vice President’s 2024 and 2025 Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN) that she jointly filed with her husband, Manases Carpio, presented as evidence of the prosecution earlier showed that Gencorp Industries Inc., formerly known as Timesquare Bee Foods Corp. and Great Jolly Times Food, is one of her business interests.

articles.title: Cebu-based shipping firm denies hand in cigarette smuggling
articles.summary: Cebu-based shipping firm Gothong Southern has denied involvement in the recently reported smuggling of P13 billion worth of cigarettes into the country.

blocks.text: Published November 11, 2026 11:48am
Cebu-based shipping firm Gothong Southern has denied involvement in the recently reported smuggling of P13 billion worth of cigarettes into the country.
The company said it is not being probed in connection with the issue.

"In light of recent reports concerning the transportation of foreign cigarettes in alleged violation of customs regulations, Gothong Southern wishes to clarify that it is not currently the subject of any investigation in connection with this matter," the statement issued on Tuesday read.
"We respect due process and the authorities' role in establishing the facts," it added.
The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has filed charges against 13 individuals linked to the smuggling of cigarettes from China.

The bureau said the suspects will face charges for violation of the Agricultural Economic Sabotage Act after over 60 container vans carrying the smuggled cigarettes were found across several ports in Cebu.
The NBI also said it has filed cases against the big fishes in the case.
Moreover, the Gothong Southern assured that it is committed to moving the economy forward "with honest, accountability, and integrity."
"Our purpose is to move the economy forward through honest and lawful trade," it said. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Fired nurse raises question of trans discrimination versus sex-based rights at appeal hearing
articles.summary: Amy Hamm is a former B.C. nurse who was fired after a discipline panel found comments she made while off-duty were discriminatory against transgender people.

image.caption: Former B.C. nurse Amy Hamm is appealing a disciplinary ruling from the province's nursing regulator that found that comments she made while off duty discriminated against transgender people. (Amy Hamm/X)

blocks.text: British Columbia
Amy Hamm is a former B.C. nurse who was fired after a discipline panel found comments she made while off-duty were discriminatory against transgender people.
Amy Hamm was fired after regulator found she made discriminatory comments against transgender people

The hearing for a former registered nurse, who is challenging a disciplinary decision that found she made discriminatory and derogatory statements about transgender people while off-duty, began Tuesday in Vancouver.
Amy Hamm brought the appeal after she was suspended, then fired, from Vancouver Coastal Health and ordered to pay nearly $94,000 in costs.

The sanctions resulted from a disciplinary hearing by the B.C. College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) that found, on four occasions, Hamm committed unprofessional conduct related to statements she made on online platforms while identifying herself as a nurse.
In the appeal petition, Hamm is described as prolific writer and a "long-time advocate of women's rights, particularly with respect to the adverse impact of gender ideology on such rights."

items: B.C. nurse suspended by college, asked to pay $94K in costs for comments about transgender people

blocks.text: Hamm's lawyer Lisa Bildy said in her opening statement that Hamm accepts that a nurse can be disciplined for off-duty comments and that transgender people are a vulnerable group.
She said the appeal fundamentally comes down to the question of a regulator's jurisdiction.

"When a public debate is still alive in our legislatures, in our courts and in the courts of comparable democracy, may a professional regulator decide which side is correct and then discipline a professional who is on the other side? We say it may not," said Bildy.

items: Fired B.C. nurse launches human rights complaints, says constitutional advocacy group

blocks.text: Bildy highlighted examples of what she claimed were inconsistencies in the panel's findings of discrimination.
She said a personal essay Hamm wrote containing the line "woman is not a feeling, woman just is" was found by the BCCNM panel to be "discriminatory erasure."
In another instance Hamm wrote "men cannot become women," which was also found to be discriminatory.
Bildy gave exampoles of similar statements made by Hamm that panel found were not discriminatory, including, "we believe most Canadians recognize woman as a biological reality rather than a feeling."

The lawyer said the inconsistencies highlight errors in how the panel defined discrimination under the law. She also said that the panel mistook Hamm's advocacy for women's sex-based rights as misconduct.
"This is the heart of the appeal," said Bildy. "The panel made a determination that you cannot advocate for sex-based rights without including transgender women."
Worked for 13 years
Bildy was interrupted a number of times by Justice Jacqueline Hughes, who said the lawyer was making arguments that were "untethered" to her pleadings.
Hamm is a single mother of two who worked as a nurse and nurse educator for 13 years until she was terminated in March of last year.

B.C.'s human rights code was amended in 2016 to include protections against discrimination based on gender identity or expression, while the federal human rights and criminal codes were updated the following year.

items: LifeLabs in B.C. ordered to pay $32K for misgendering transgender, non-binary patients: Human Rights Tribunal

blocks.text: Hamm has filed two complaints with the B.C. Human Rights Tribunal.

The first alleges Vancouver Coastal Health discriminated against her and fired her based on her political beliefs. The second, against the College of Nurses and Midwives, claims regulatory authorities used their power to enforce a particular world view — in this case, gender ideology.
Hamm's appeal hearing in B.C. Supreme Court is scheduled to continue on Wednesday and Thursday.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Karin Larsen is a former Olympian and award-winning sports broadcaster who covers news and sports for CBC Vancouver.

articles.title: Kennedys sue to block Trump's arch, arguing it would cast shadow on JFK's grave
articles.summary: Nine members of the political dynasty say the 250ft structure would cast a shadow on gravesites.

blocks.text: Image source, Reuters
An artist's rendering of Trump's proposed arch near Arlington Cemetery
The family of former US President John F Kennedy has sued to block construction of a triumphal arch that President Donald Trump plans to build in the nation's capital.

Nine members of the political dynasty argue the 250ft (76m) structure would block the view of Kennedy's grave, as well as the graves of thousands of veterans buried at Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia.
Last week, a US judge temporarily halted the project on the heels of a vote allowing construction to proceed.
The White House said it was "unfortunate" to see that some members of the Kennedy family had joined litigation against an arch "intended to honor our heroes who rest in Arlington Cemetery".
"The judiciary should not be abused to politicize a structure designed to unite our nation," White House spokesman Davis R Ingle said in a statement to the BBC.
"We will continue making the case for this beautiful and fitting monument and are confident we will be fully vindicated as this litigation proceeds," he added.
Watch: Protesters demonstrate against Trump’s proposed arch
Last week the project won approval from the National Capital Planning Commission.
But US District Judge Tanya Chutkan then ruled there should be a 14-day pause before any work can start on the arch as litigation plays out.

The Kennedy family filed its complaint under a joint lawsuit brought by the state of Virginia and Washington DC seeking to block construction, arguing that the arch will damage "historically significant sightlines" if erected at the gateway of the cemetery.
The plaintiffs include seven children of Robert and Ethel Kennedy, as well as their grandson - former Democrat congressman Joe Kennedy - and Ted Kennedy's son Edward Kennedy Jr.
It does not include Trump cabinet official Robert F Kennedy Jr, who leads the Department of Health and Human Services.
Their motion moves to intervene in two other lawsuits filed by conservationists and veterans seeking to halt the construction.

They say the arch would be a "permanent denigration" of the gravesites and that the Kennedy offspring "would never again be able to appreciate both sites as they always have before, and as the Kennedy family always intended".

blocks.caption: Satellite image with 3D buildings visible showing a model of the proposed Triumphal Arch in Washington DC, positioned south of the Potomac River at the end of Arlington Memorial Bridge. The Lincoln Memorial, on the other side of the bridge, the Washington Monument, further to the east, and the Wh…

blocks.text: The Kennedy family argues the structure "will permanently cast shadows over and damage historically significant sightlines to the existing gravesites and memorials established in the Kennedy family's honor" at the cemetery.
The structure would also "fundamentally alter the experience of visiting the gravesites", including the memorials of hundreds of thousands of US veterans, the Kennedys said.
The complaint said that the National Park Service and Interior Department authorised construction on 5 November 2026 without the necessary congressional approval.
The so-called Arc de Trump is one of the president's efforts to remake the capital city and is meant to commemorate the country's 250th anniversary.
Last year, he also added his name to the Kennedy Center, a major Washington DC cultural institution named in honour of JFK.
Trump's name remained on the facade for six months until the addition was ruled illegal and removed.

articles.title: [In This Economy] The Philippines has entered stagflation territory
articles.summary: There’s a lot of lost growth to catch up on, especially since many if not most of our neighbors are performing well in terms of growth

blocks.text: The Philippine economy grew by a measly 2.1% in the third quarter of 2026, the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) reported on Monday, November 9. That’s down from 4% in the same quarter last year and 2.4% in the second quarter, after revisions.

blocks.caption: Quarterly GDP growth, year-on-year, In This Economy, graph

blocks.text: This is a deeply disappointing result. Growth fell 0.9 percentage point short of the 2.7% median forecast in a BusinessWorld poll of economists. And we’ve now had two quarters of unusually weak growth alongside high inflation. By my own calculations, we’ve entered stagflation territory.

How much did the economy grow from the second to the third quarter itself? Once you account for the usual seasonal ups and downs, gross domestic product (GDP) grew by just 0.1%. In other words, the amount of goods and services we produced barely changed from one quarter to the next.

That leaves growth at about 2.5% for the first nine months of 2026. To reach even the bottom of the government’s reduced target of 3.5% to 4.5% for 2026, the economy would have to grow by 6.3% in the last quarter. Where would that growth come from? Your guess is as good as mine.

Let’s start with household spending, which accounts for nearly three-fourths of the economy. It grew by just 2.4% from a year ago, after adjusting for inflation. Spending on food and nonalcoholic drinks grew by only 1.6%. Spending on transport fell by 5.3%, its second straight quarterly decline from a year earlier.

One reason for weaker spending is very high inflation, which reached 7.8% in October, up from 7.2% in September. October falls outside the GDP report, which covers July to September, but it gives us an early indication of the squeeze on households going into the final quarter.

Meanwhile, agriculture, forestry, and fishing contracted by 4.8%, and industry was essentially flat. Services grew by 3.7% and contributed about 2.5 percentage points to overall growth. That’s more than the economy’s 2.1% growth because losses elsewhere ate into those gains.

blocks.caption: Philippine GDP breakdown, expenditure side, graph

blocks.text: The PSA reported that total investment, or gross capital formation, fell by just 0.2%. But when I broke down the numbers, the near-flat figure concealed a much bigger decline. Fixed investment, which includes things like buildings and equipment, fell by 4.4%. Spending on durable equipment alone fell by 7.8%.

What made up most of the difference? Inventories, or goods that businesses hold in stock: in the third quarter last year, businesses ran down their inventories by P14 billion. This year, they added P37 billion, both measured at 2018 prices. That swing of P51 billion added roughly 0.9 percentage point to GDP growth.
The national accounts tell us stocks went up. But we need more evidence to know whether firms were building them up deliberately or had trouble selling what they already had.

The construction figures also deserve a closer look. Government construction fell by 15.1%. That’s a smaller drop than the 33.4% contraction in the second quarter, but still quite substantial. Corporate construction grew by just 0.3%, while construction by households and nonprofit institutions grew by 1.1%.

Interestingly, government consumption grew by 6.8% in the same quarter. That covers the cost of providing public services, including salaries and operating expenses. Public works are counted separately as investment. The government spent more on running its agencies and less on building things.

Perhaps most consequentially, the drastic slowdown is pulling us farther from our pre-pandemic path. In my analysis, actual seasonally adjusted output in the third quarter was P5.95 trillion at 2018 prices, or about 22% below where it would be if the pre-pandemic trend had continued. It gives us a sense of how much ground we have yet to make up.

When asked by journalists, Socioeconomic Planning Secretary Arsenio Balisacan said he would wait until year-end before thinking of stagflation, the combination of weak economic growth and high inflation. So I looked at how often the two have occurred together in the Philippines since 2000.

blocks.caption: Philippines, stagflation, graph

blocks.text: In a paper I’m writing, I use two tests. First, inflation must average more than 5% that quarter. Second, the economy’s growth from a year earlier must fall more than two percentage points below its average pace over a 10-year stretch ending in that quarter. Think of an economy that usually grows at 5%. Under this rule, growth below 3% would count as unusually weak.

The second and third quarters of 2026 both pass those tests. The third quarter is the clearer case. The second quarter was so close to the line that a small revision to the GDP figures could change the result.

Both quarters still qualify if I leave the 2020 lockdown slump out of the growth average, or if I leave out the 2021 reopening bounce as well. Under all three versions, this is the first back-to-back pair of qualifying quarters in the data going back to 2000.
We’re already in stagflation territory, but let’s see if we’re still there by year-end.

There’s a lot of lost growth to catch up on, especially since many if not most of our neighbors are performing well in terms of growth. In fact, it’s quite embarrassing to be chairing the ASEAN this year while our growth figures are relatively dismal.

blocks.caption: GDP growth, selected Asian economies

blocks.text: For its part, the Marcos administration can start by explaining which vetted public works it can get moving again, when workers can expect those projects to resume, and how it will keep another round of questionable projects out of the pipeline.
For the rest of us, we haven’t felt the full headwinds yet, what with the effects of Super El Niño on inflation and growth lasting until early 2027. Prepare for tougher times ahead. – Rappler.com

Jan Carlo “JC” Punongbayan, PhD, is an associate professor at the University of the Philippines School of Economics. His professional experience includes the Securities and Exchange Commission, the World Bank Office in Manila, the Far Eastern University Public Policy Center, and the National Economic and Development Authority. JC writes a weekly economics column for Rappler. He is also co-founder of UsapangEcon.com and co-host of Usapang Econ Podcast.

His first book, False Nostalgia: The Marcos “Golden Age” Myths and How to Debunk Them, was published by Ateneo de Manila University Press in February 2023. His second book, Twin Plagues: How Duterte and COVID-19 Wrecked the Philippine Economy, was published by Penguin Random House SEA in June 2026. Follow him on Instagram (@jcpunongbayan).

articles.title: Israel: Eisenkot proposes October 7 probe as new Knesset sworn in
articles.summary: Ex-IDF chief Gadi Eisenkot has yet to forge a coalition that would allow him to replace Benjamin Netanyahu, despite the new Knesset being dominated by the critics of the current prime minister.

image.caption: Eisenkot's coalition also wants to impose term limits on Israeli prime ministersImage: Ohad Zwigenberg/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: The parliamentary bloc led by Israeli ex-military leader Gadi Eisenkot announced a slew of initiatives on Tuesday targeting the legacy of current Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as the new Israeli Parliament, or Knesset, was sworn in.
Israel held a parliamentary election on October 27.
Eisenkot's bloc wants government inquiry into October 7 attack

Eisenkot's centrist Yashar Party and allied parties are seeking an official government inquiry into the Hamas-led terror attacks on October 7, 2023, which killed some 1,200 people in Israel and resulted in another 251 hostages being taken into Gaza.
The attack, which occurred on Netanyahu's watch, was the single deadliest day for Jewish people since the Holocaust.

Some media outlets had reported that Netanyahu received warnings from Egypt and the UAE ahead of the October 7 assault. The Israeli prime minister denied the claims and said he would sue for defamation over the publications.

In addition to an October 7 probe, the anti-Netanyahu opposition is also seeking to impose term limits on the office of prime minister and aims to reverse the controversial efforts made by the Netanyahu government to reforming the judiciary. Eisenkot's bloc is also seeking to depose Knesset speaker Amir Ohana, a Netanyahu ally.

blocks.caption: The new Knesset has 33 female members — the highest share since Israel's founding in 1948Image: Ilia Yefimovich/AFP

blocks.text: "We will act for all citizens of Israel, those who voted for us and those who did not, out of deep commitment," Eisenkot said prior to the swearing-in of the new Knesset. He pledged to "form a national-emergency government as quickly as possible."
Both Netanyahu and Eisenkot bloc short of Knesset majority
Israeli President Isaac Herzog has given Eisenkot a mandate to try to form a government within six weeks.
Eisenkot's coalition bloc landed 48 seats in the recent election, whereas Netanyahu's bloc received 53 seats. But neither bloc has enough seats to form a majority in the 120-seat Knesset.

Arab parties garnered a record 19 out of 120 seats in the new Knesset. During the swearing-in ceremony, far-right Israeli politician Itamar Ben-Gvir harassed Arab-Israeli lawmaker Yousef Jabareen in the Knesset chamber

Eisenkot's bloc could choose to align with the Arab parties to form a government, but Avigdor Lieberman and his right-wing Yisrael Beitenu party oppose the idea. Yisrael Beitenu, which won seven seats in the new Knesset, is a part of the Eisenkot bloc.
Israeli president asks Eisenkot to form government
Netanyahu urges national unity government to confront Iran

Netanyahu, in a speech to the Knesset, called for a national unity government — a proposal which has been ruled out by Eisenkot. The incumbent head of government lashed out at Arab parties and accused them of backing Israel's destruction while saying the national unity government is necessary to confront Iran.

"In the very near future, we're going to be confronted by international pressure to accept a nuclear-armed Iran and the preservation of this terror regime that seeks to annihilate us," Netanyahu said.

Eisenkot condemned Netanyahu's remarks, whereas Yair Golan, the leader of the left-wing Democrats party, walked out during Netanyahu's speech. The Democrats have eight seats and are part of the Eisenkot bloc.
"Netanyahu is struggling to accept that the Israeli public fired him. Now he is lying and inciting against the Arab public in an attempt to cling to power by force," Golan said on X.
How Israel's PM Netanyahu holds on to power

If Eisenkot fails to form a government, Israeli President Herzog could choose another lawmaker, presumably Netanyahu, to cobble together a coalition. The 77-year-old Netanyahu first took power in 1996 and has had three separate stints as the Israeli head of government.
Netanyahu is now the longest-serving prime minister in Israeli history.

articles.title: Mike Hammer star and stage actor Stacy Keach dead at 85
articles.summary: Stacy Keach, one of America's finest stage actors who became best known for playing scruffy private eye Mike Hammer on TV and whose career was nearly derailed after he was imprisoned in 1984 for…

image.caption: Actor Stacy Keach, seen in a February 2003 photo, has died at the age of 85. (Kevin Winter/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

Stacy Keach, one of America's finest stage actors who became best known for playing scruffy private eye Mike Hammer on TV and whose career was nearly derailed after he was imprisoned in 1984 for trying to smuggle cocaine into Britain, died Tuesday. He was 85.
Keach died at his home in Poland, following a long battle with heart problems

Keach died at home in Magdalenka, Poland, "after a long and difficult battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure," his wife, Malgosia Tomassi Keach, said in a statement. Keach had previously suffered a heart attack onstage in Chicago in June 2017.

Though he was considered a preeminent interpreter of Shakespeare and a favourite of such legendary directors as John Huston, Keach was indelibly linked with his take on the hard-boiled Hammer, the fictitious TV private detective created by crime novelist Mickey Spillane.

Unwilling to do the same thing over and over, Keach left behind a crazy quilt of roles, playing a stoner cop on film, King Lear onstage and also narrating World's Most Amazing Videos on TV. He played a deranged colonel in The Ninth Configuration (also known as Twinkle, Twinkle Killer Kane), led the TV show Titus, had a role in Alexander Payne's Oscar-nominated drama Nebraska and played a New York archbishop in a recurring role on the CBS police drama Blue Bloods. Last year, he had an excellent turn as George Clooney's bitter father in Jay Kelly.

"My objective was to have as varied a selection of roles as possible. It probably did hurt my career," he told New York magazine in 2012. "My choices have had a cost attached to it. But I've gotten to play Hamlet, and Richard III, and King Lear, and I would not give that up for anything."
'One of the greats'

Actor Lou Diamond Phillips, who played Keach's son in the 2008 TV movie Lone Rider, said in a post on X that Keach was a "consummate actor, gracious, giving and incredibly kind even while he had the presence of a smoldering volcano. One of the greats. Proud to have shared some frames with him."
Keach, seen in April 1984, was one of America's finest stage actors. (Daily Express/Hulton Archive/Getty Images)

Keach played French painter Julien Mistral in the CBS miniseries Mistral's Daughter, a Russian prince in the miniseries version of Judith Krantz's novel Princess Daisy, Barabbas in Franco Zeffirelli's Jesus of Nazareth and Maj. Jonas Steele in The Blue and the Gray. He won a Golden Globe playing Ernest Hemingway in a six-hour miniseries, for which he gained 35 pounds.

Keach earned a Tony Award nomination for his portrayal of Buffalo Bill in the Broadway play Indians, played Edmund opposite Lee J. Cobb in King Lear on Broadway and had other onstage roles there in The Kentucky Cycle in 1993, The Country Wife in 1965 and Other Desert Cities in 2011.

He also headed the national touring company cast of Frost/Nixon, portraying the fallen president, and went on tour with Sleuth with Maxwell Caulfield as his co-star. He starred in a 2006 production of King Lear at the Goodman Theatre in Chicago and returned in 2017 for Pamplona, a one-man show about Hemingway, where he collapsed onstage, leading to the run's cancellation.
'Lowest moment' was prison

While he was still doing Mickey Spillane's Mike Hammer (later titled The New Mike Hammer), Keach was arrested in 1984 at London's Heathrow Airport after trying to smuggle 1.3 ounces of cocaine concealed in an aerosol shaving cream can and elsewhere in his luggage. Also arrested was his secretary.
Stacy Keach and his wife Malgosia Tomassi Keach pose for a photo at a premiere in 2006. (Lucas Jackson/The Associated Press)

"As my sentence was read — nine months in prison — I felt like someone had kicked me in the groin with lead cleats," he wrote in his 2013 book, All in All: An Actor's Life On and Off the Stage. He added: "It was the lowest moment of my life."

He was handcuffed and taken to prison, a cell the size of a closet and where an orange plastic bucket would serve as his toilet. Before he went inside, an officer asked him to autograph a copy of the book The Blue and the Gray.

The then-44-year-old actor was sent to Reading Prison, a medium-security lockup, because authorities felt a minimum-security jail would have provided too easy access for reporters. He was released after six months.

In his book, Keach wrote that while in prison he got warm letters from Gregory Peck, Burt Reynolds, Roger Moore and Al Pacino. He was put in charge of showing a movie one Sunday per month and recalls once picking his own, The Long Riders. He said the experience was "very lonely, very depressing, very sad. I spent a lot of my time trying to re-evaluate my own stupidity."

After prison, he narrated the TV documentary High on the Job, and testified before Congress, telling a House panel how he first became hooked on cocaine in the mid-1970s. "There is no greater imprisonment than that of being dependent on a chemical substance for one's existence," he testified.

Keach took his warnings to college campuses and rehab centres. He also married Polish actor Malgosia Tomassi, whom he met when she appeared in the Hammer series. He said he treasured her photos and letters behind bars.
Married 4 times
Keach, who was married four times, is survived by Malgosia, and his children, Shannon and Karolina.

His first role after his release was in the CBS movie, Intimate Strangers with Teri Garr, and it became the third-highest rated TV movie of the 1985-86 season. His next film, The Return of Mickey Spillane's Mike Hammer, also played well, and then the Mike Hammer series, which had been on the production shelf since his arrest, was given a slot on CBS' 1986-87 schedule.

Many years later, in the TV series Prison Break that aired from 2005-2007, Keach played a prison warden and said he tried to model his character after his real-life warden in England, whom he said had great compassion and wanted to help inmates rehabilitate themselves.
Born in Savannah, Ga., Keach was the son of actors who met at Northwestern University. Keach attended the University of California, Berkeley, where he earned degrees in English and dramatic art.

articles.title: Over 23,000 personnel to secure ASEAN Summit 2026
articles.summary: More than 23,000 personnel will be deployed to secure the 49th ASEAN Summit in Metro Manila, according to authorities on Wednesday.

blocks.text: Published November 11, 2026 11:27am
More than 23,000 personnel will be deployed to secure the 49th ASEAN Summit in Metro Manila, according to authorities on Wednesday.

ASEAN 2026 Security Task Force commander Police Lieutenant General Nery Vincent Ignacio said a total of 23,154 personnel will be fielded to secure designated routes, summit venues, billeting hotels, and other concerned areas.

“For the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summit, it is my honor to present a formidable total force of 23,154 personnel to secure all designated routes, summit venues, building hotels and surrounding areas of responsibility,” he said during the send-off ceremony at Quirino Grandstand in Manila.
“Of this number, 20,079 personnel come from the National Capital Region, supported by the 3,075 personnel from our multi-agency support component,” he added.

These include personnel from the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP), Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP), Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA), emergency preparedness and response units, and local traffic units from Pasay, Parañaque, Makati, Taguig, and Manila.

The security deployment will be supported by around 4,000 civil disturbance management equipment, 15 trucks and buses, more than 1,000 motorcycles, and over 300 mobile cars. With additional vehicles from Unified 911, the total number of mobile cars will reach more than 500.
He added that the deployment will also include ambulances, canine units, high-speed tactical watercraft, and 157 additional support and response vehicles from partner agencies.
Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla said the government had acquired 550 new vehicles, 600 motorcycles, and 150 ambulances for the ASEAN security operations.
He added that 1,500 new fire trucks from South Korea are expected to arrive.
Remulla urged deployed personnel to follow their orders, remain at their assigned posts, and be prepared for any eventuality.
"Do your utmost. In the next few hours, in the next 72 hours, do your utmost.Follow your orders, obey your commands, be at your post, and be ready for any eventuality," Remulla said.
Philippine National Police (PNP) chief Police General Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. said authorities had been preparing for the ASEAN activities for almost a year.
He said the government has accounted for 639 activities, with 159 remaining as of Wednesday. The main events are scheduled for the third week of November.
According to him, the ASEAN Summit is expected to be attended by 23 leaders along with thousands of their staff members and observers.
“Ngayon pa lang, nagko-congratulate na ako sa ating mga security forces who have drafted and played an important role in making this activity peaceful and will make this activity peaceful,” he said.
The summit proper will begin on Sunday, November 15. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: PNP: 300K wanted persons, including Bato, Zaldy Co, Bantag, Atong Ang, remain at large
articles.summary: The Philippine National Police (PNP) is pursuing around 300,000 wanted persons nationwide as the organization targets zero backlog.

blocks.text: Published November 11, 2026 11:21am
The Philippine National Police (PNP) is pursuing around 300,000 wanted persons nationwide as the organization targets zero backlog.
This figure includes high-profile individuals such as Senator Ronald dela Rosa, former lawmaker Zaldy Co, former Bureau of Corrections chief Gerald Bantag, and businessman Atong Ang.

“We are confident that we can achieve this goal because we have already shown that sustained and determined action can significantly reduce the number of wanted persons,” PNP chief Police General Jose Melencio Nartatez said in a statement on Tuesday.
“We will not be satisfied with reducing the backlog since our ultimate objective is to bring it down to zero,” he added.
Nartatez stressed that the campaign against fugitives covers all individuals with outstanding arrest warrants, regardless of their status or position.

The PNP is aiming to bring the number of remaining wanted persons down to zero through sustained police operations, intelligence gathering, and closer coordination with other law enforcement agencies.

When Nartatez assumed the PNP leadership on August 26, 2025, the PNP said around 500,000 wanted persons were listed in its database. The figure has since dropped by around 200,000 following the arrest of fugitives over the past 14 months.
Around 300,000 wanted persons are still remaining.
In October, 8,839 wanted persons were arrested nationwide, including 2,353 classified as most wanted persons and 6,486 other wanted individuals.
The National Capital Region Police Office recorded the highest number of arrests with 1,641, followed by Police Regional Office (RPO) 3 with 1,503 and PRO 4A with 1,317. — Joviland Rita/RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Slovak foreign minister to open embassy in Manila
articles.summary: Slovakia will formally open its embassy in Manila during a visit by Foreign Minister Juraj Blanár on November 12-15, the Department of Foreign Affairs said on Wednesday, November 11.

blocks.text: November 11, 2026 | 11:16am
Slovakia's Foreign Minister Juraj Blanar looks on during a joint press conference with Poland's Foreign Minister after their meeting at Foreign Ministry building in Warsaw on March 13, 2025.
AFP / Wojtek Radwanski

MANILA, Philippines — Slovakia will formally open its embassy in Manila during a visit by Foreign Minister Juraj Blanár on November 12-15, the Department of Foreign Affairs said on Wednesday, November 11.
During the visit, Blanár will also sign a declaration depositing Slovakia’s instrument of accession to the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia, ASEAN’s 1976 peace pact, the DFA said.
It is the first official visit by a Slovak foreign minister to the Philippines since 2015.
Blanár, who is traveling with a business delegation, will also meet Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro on Thursday, November 12.
On Friday, November 13, the minister is set to meet Trade Secretary Cristina Aldeguer-Roque and give the keynote speech at a Philippines-Slovak business forum.

The 1976 treaty commits its parties to respect for sovereignty, the principle of non-interference, and the peaceful settlement of disputes. Countries outside the region have been able to join since 1987, but only with the consent of all ASEAN members.
Miloš Koterec, Slovakia’s first resident ambassador, presented his credentials to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in February.
The Philippines and Slovakia established diplomatic relations in 1993.
Lazaro and Blanár last met in April in Brunei, at the ASEAN-EU Ministerial Meeting.
